Chiprovtsi Carpets

600 Years of Tradition

The History of
Chiprovtsi Carpets

A story woven in wool — from medieval Bulgaria to the UNESCO World Heritage list.

Origins in the Medieval Kingdom

The art of carpet weaving in Chiprovtsi traces its roots to the 14th and 15th centuries, during the final years of the Second Bulgarian Empire. Nestled in the Balkan mountain foothills of Northwest Bulgaria, the town of Chiprovtsi developed a unique weaving culture influenced by both local Bulgarian folk tradition and contact with Saxon miners who settled in the region during the Middle Ages.

The earliest Chiprovtsi carpets were woven on simple horizontal looms, primarily for domestic use — to warm earthen floors, to decorate walls, and to serve as ceremonial gifts at weddings and births. Patterns were passed from mother to daughter, never written down, living entirely in the hands and memory of the weavers.

Did you know? Chiprovtsi carpets are distinguished by their double-sided flatweave technique — the pattern is identical on both sides, a feat that requires extraordinary skill.

The Golden Age — 16th to 17th Century

The craft flourished under Ottoman rule, finding its most productive era during the 16th and 17th centuries. Chiprovtsi carpets became valued trade goods exported to Dubrovnik, Venice, and across the Habsburg Empire. It was during this period that the most iconic patterns crystallised — the Ptitsi (Birds), the Bakam (Double Diamond), and the Shareni Lenti (Coloured Bands) — patterns that remain in production today, virtually unchanged in their essential geometry.

14th–15th C.

Origins

Carpet weaving begins in Chiprovtsi. Patterns are passed orally, mother to daughter, never written down.

16th–17th C.

Golden Age of Trade

Chiprovtsi carpets are exported to Venice, Dubrovnik and Vienna. The most iconic patterns — Birds, Bacam, Coloured Bands — are born.

1688

The Chiprovtsi Uprising

A failed rebellion against Ottoman rule leads to the town's destruction. Many weavers flee to Wallachia and Transylvania, spreading the craft abroad.

18th–19th C.

Rebirth and Revival

The town is slowly rebuilt. By the 19th century Chiprovtsi carpets appear at European craft exhibitions.

1927

First Cooperative Founded

The first carpet-weaving cooperative is established in Chiprovtsi, standardising quality for export markets.

2014

UNESCO Recognition

The traditional craft of Chiprovtsi carpet weaving is inscribed on the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.

The Craft Today

Today approximately 200 active weavers continue the tradition in and around Chiprovtsi. Each carpet is woven on a traditional vertical loom using hand-spun wool from local Balkan sheep. The annual Chiprovtsi Carpet Fair, held each September, draws buyers and collectors from across Europe — a living demonstration that this ancient art is not merely preserved, but alive and evolving.

UNESCO Inscription 2014: The traditional craft of Chiprovtsi carpet-weaving was inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, recognising it as a living tradition of outstanding cultural significance.

Our Story

About Kovyor

A small team with a big love for Bulgarian heritage — bringing authentic Chiprovtsi carpets to homes around the world.

Who We Are

Kovyor (Bulgarian for "carpet") was born from a simple frustration: the most beautiful carpets in the world, made in the mountain town of Chiprovtsi in Northwest Bulgaria, were nearly impossible to buy outside of Bulgaria. We set out to change that.

We are a small, family-connected team based between Varna and Chiprovtsi. We work directly with the weavers — no middlemen, no wholesale warehouses — which means every carpet you see in our catalog has been personally selected from an artisan's loom.

🧵

Direct from Artisans

We work directly with Chiprovtsi weavers, paying fair prices that reflect the true value of months of hand-labour.

🌿

Natural Materials

All carpets use hand-spun Balkan wool. Many weavers we work with are returning to traditional plant-based dyes.

🏛

UNESCO Heritage

Every purchase supports a living UNESCO-recognised craft tradition — one of Bulgaria's greatest cultural treasures.

📦

Carefully Shipped

Each carpet is hand-rolled and wrapped in protective fabric before shipping. We pack with the same care the weaver wove.

Our Mission

Our mission is straightforward: connect the hands that make with the homes that love. We believe buying a Chiprovtsi carpet is not just an interior design decision — it is an act of cultural preservation.

When you lay a Sluntse carpet in your hallway or hang a Ptitsi carpet on your wall, you are keeping alive a 600-year-old conversation between a weaver and the world.

The Weavers

The women who weave Chiprovtsi carpets are not factory workers — they are artists who have inherited a visual language. Many learned at their grandmother's loom. Some have been weaving for over 40 years. Their hands carry knowledge that cannot be found in any book.

We visit Chiprovtsi regularly, we know the weavers by name, and we are proud to call several of them friends. When you ask us about a specific carpet, we can often tell you exactly who made it and how long it took.

Shipping &
Return Policy

We want your carpet to arrive safely and for you to love it. Here is everything about how we ship and what happens if you don't.

Shipping

All carpets are hand-rolled, wrapped in breathable fabric, and placed in a sturdy cardboard tube or flat box. We ship from Chiprovtsi / Varna, Bulgaria via tracked courier services.

BulgariaSpeedy / Econt1–2 business daysFree

Rest of WorldFedEx / DHL7–14 business daysEUR45 (free over EUR300)

Free shipping on all orders over EUR300. Please allow 1–3 business days for preparation before dispatch.

Customs & Import Duties

For orders within the EU, no customs duties apply. For orders outside the EU, import duties and taxes may be charged by your country's customs authority. These charges are the buyer's responsibility and are not included in our prices.

Return Policy

We offer a 30-day return policy from the date of delivery.

How to Return

  1. Email us at hello@kovyor.bg within 30 days of receiving your order.
  2. Include your order number and a brief description of the reason for return.
  3. We will send you a return authorisation and packaging instructions.
  4. Roll and wrap the carpet carefully in the original packaging if possible.
  5. Ship the carpet back using a tracked service. Return shipping costs are the buyer's responsibility unless the item was faulty.

Refunds

Once we receive and inspect the returned carpet, we will issue a full refund within 5–7 business days to your original payment method. Carpets must be returned clean, undamaged, and unaltered.

Non-Returnable Items

  • Custom-sized or made-to-order carpets (unless faulty)
  • Carpets that show signs of use, washing, or damage caused after delivery

Damaged or Incorrect Items

If your carpet arrives damaged, please contact us within 48 hours with photos. We will arrange a free return and send a replacement or issue a full refund.
